159866.overview:
Defence Force is a clone of the game Defender: a side scrolling shoot'em up where you have to defend humans.

Humanity has been almost totally destroyed. You are a pilot of the Defence Force and you have to kill waves of aliens coming from both sides of the screen. You will meet 16 different types of aliens, some moving only in one direction, others trying to crash in to your ship, others dividing in smaller ships when shot, and some are even invisible. Radar shows you where enemies (even invisible ones) and humans are located on the level.

The Vulturae type of alien ships should be you primary target as they try to abduct humans to transform them into Assassins (which will try to crash in your ship). For any alien wave, if there is a time where there are no humans left, you will be warped into the Astral Plains, where all remaining enemies are turned into Wraith, a fast skull-looking ship which tries to bump your ship away. To help you to survive, you can activate shields, the screen is then blue and you are invincible.. for a few seconds (6 seconds on the first wave, only 1 second in the more difficult high levels).

The player uses the cursor keys to control the ship. There is no fire button: each time you press the move key, the ship shoots a laser beam.

173492.overview: Dallas is a simulation game where the player takes control of a company in the oil business. The aim of the game is to make enough money in order to take over the rivalling company Euing Associates. The game shows a map over Texas and is played by choosing from a text menu and entering coordinates on the map. To develop an oil field the player can make seismic surveys to find good spots and then bids on concessions. Once land has been acquired the player has to first move a rig before drilling for oil. If oil is found production facilities can be built before a pipeline to Dallas is laid. To finance the constructions loans can be sought. Problems that can hamper progress include blow outs, tornadoes, accidents, increased taxes and crude oil surplus.

175405.overview: A Damsel in Distress needs rescuing by yourself, and so in this single screen platform game, you must get around the screen to reach her over various levels. As you move around the screen, you must collect all the objects on the screen before you can get to the Damsel. You are unable to fall or move off a platform from any height, so you must follow a route that allows you to jump from platform-to-platform to collect all the items. There are various creatures that are on-screen and when you land on their platform, they start moving and need avoiding. Umbrellas can be used to move down to lower platforms and if you fall or touch a creature then you lose one of three lives, and you have to start the level again.

175406.overview: Dam Buster (Dambuster on the title screen) is a flight combat simulator developed and published by IJK Software in 1984.

175544.overview:
Ostensibly a Donkey Kong clone, Dinky Kong isn't a straight variant of the arcade original, instead the latter 'rivet' levels are incorporated into the first level so that you must dodge the barrels while also doubling back to ensure you've removed the rivets that make the structure unsound and will eventually lead to a win.

Removing rivets will result in barrels falling through them so it becomes a little easier to plan once you get yourself into a spot where you can better judge the direction a barrel will travel.  Missing rivets, however, do provide another hazard and you must leap over the newly created holes to avoid falling to your death.

175545.overview: Guide Max the Mutt to his long buried bones, but watch out for the perilous rat holes. Win the race or be eaten by the deadly rats.

175588.overview: Coax the monsters down holes that have been dug in the walkways, without being killed yourself. There are bags of gold stashed at the top left of the screen. You can get bonus points by carrying the bags down to the bank, at the bottom right of the screen. You move twice as fast as the monsters except when you are carrying a bag of gold. The oxygen slowly is exhausted show by a bar at the top of the screen. To kill a monster, you must dig a hole, coax a monster to fill the hole and fill it in before the monster escapes in 10 seconds. Red monsters need to fall one level, green 2 and yellow need to fall 3 levels.

175651.overview: Dracula's Revenge is a simple platform/shooter game for the Oric-1 and Oric Atmos computers. It was developed and published by Softek in 1983.

175652.overview: Play a nice game of checkers against the computer opponent. A very competent version of draughts. There is a a number of options available regarding colours, skill levels and creating custom situations. Graphics and sound are obviously limited but perfectly functional and everything has been well laid out. If you like draughts, this is a good version to play.

175795.overview: White Doggy is running on the linear forest road to reach his kennel. The screen scrolls from left to right to simulate this event seen from a third-person perspective. The road is full of different obstacles, and it is the player's task to avoid them. The obstacles vary from traps, barriers, logs, pits, etc. to a truck scattering the debris or a wolf running in the opposite direction. Doggy may be controlled to jump and move on the road up and down. The dog's energy is gradually exhausting while it is running. Bones scattered on the road may be collected to refill the dog's energy. If the energy is vanished or with each obstacle struck, the dog loses a life. There are five dog lives at the start. The best scores are stored in a high score table.

175874.overview: You will find yourself on any floor of a tower which counts 60 (and a ground floor). You will know which floor you are on are and you will see yourself evolving on the plan of this floor. Your goal is to find a fabulous treasure which is located somewhere leaves in the tower... But to take the treasure, you will need to display a 4-digit secret code. If you manage to take the treasure, you will have to keep it and exit the tower.

175877.overview:
Don Juan challenges the player to reach the fame of the legendary seducer of women.

The player starts with 1200 pounds (or 9000 francs) of wealth and 0 points on the lovometer. To increase the lovometer's score, the player must enter single keywords (verbs in infinitive). Each word represents an idea, enabling player to tell the lady about himself, pay her compliments, or make suggestions. Which words are successful depends on the girl's character. Several keywords lead to menus to specify the idea more precisely (for example, 5 menu items representing locations with different prices are shown on the word TRIP). The girl's reaction to a keyword is shown through her facial expression (smile, wink, kiss, etc.).

But seducing is not easy, because certain rules are in effect and unforeseen events can occur. The same word cannot be entered more than 3 times if it was used successfully, nor can the player see the sub-menus more than 3 times. An unsuccessful word may become successful later, however. Entering HELP or WORDS gives hints and a list of the game's vocabulary, but a fee must be paid for their use. Among the possible events are the appearance of a rival who steals the player's beloved. In addition, some tragic event may occur with the girl, such as her dog being eaten by bigger one, an acne attack, a toothache, losing her job, etc. In this case, the player should cheer her up with the right keyword.

There are 3 difficulty levels. The player wins if he obtains a score of 500 for level 1, 700 for level 2, and 800 for level 3.

216376.overview: The Dark Village Mystery is a hybrid of a text adventure and a text-based role-playing game for the Oric Computers. It was developed by Peter Shaw and released as a type-in game in the book "More Games for your Oric" in 1984.

421199.overview: Dico 5 (Spelled Dico-5 on the title screen) is a French language Mastermind clone for the Oric-1/Atmos computers. It was developed and published by Loriciels in 1983.
